description: Record types the publication validator enforces. Derived from the 2026-10-12 filing-compliance audit (18 record types) reduced to the six types that can be mechanically validated at publication time, plus Clinton's 2026-10-12 governing clarifications: Orders are NOT Matters; a Matter opens only when existing law requires; multiple Orders may belong to one Matter; standing/procedural Orders may stand alone with authority + provenance; the public docket is representative while the private canonical docket is authoritative; require only identifiers/provenance/status/linkages actually mandated by controlling law.

global_rules.human_approval: Every publication filing (all types) requires an authorization receipt naming Clinton Brown as authorizer with a content hash matching the exact filed bytes. Missing or mismatched receipt = BLOCK, no waiver.
global_rules.private_never_public: classification 'private' is always BLOCKED by this validator. Private-classified records belong on the private canonical docket, not the public repo.
global_rules.waiver_scope: Privacy-scan findings ONLY may be waived, and only by an explicit waiver entry approved_by Clinton Brown with a non-empty justification. Waived findings are still reported in the verdict output, never hidden.

correction.authority_requirements: Must cite the authority for the correction and every cited reference must resolve. The supersedes target must resolve to an existing record.
correction.correction_rules: The superseded record's file must NOT appear among the changed files (no in-place edit of superseded text). The only documented exception is a secret/PII incident handled under the PUB-M-005 precedent, which still requires Human direction and is routed to human review, never auto-passed.
correction.description: Correction / supersession. Corrections take a NEW identity with a pointer to the superseded record; the superseded text is never edited in place (Constitution Art. VIII section 5).
correction.index_coverage: changed files must include law/orders/INDEX.json (new row for the new identity)
correction.matter_rules: NO matter linkage required. If present it must resolve.

judgment.authority_requirements: Must cite the Human Judgment entry (briefing provenance where applicable). Every cited reference must resolve.
judgment.description: Human-entered Judgment (J-nnnn) as JSON per the judgment template. Judgments are durable general law; entry is Human-reserved.
judgment.index_coverage: changed files must include CURRENT_LAW.md (Active Judgments table) alongside the judgment file
judgment.matter_rules: NO matter linkage required. If present it must resolve.
judgment.notes: PROPOSED_NOT_ADOPTED instruments (e.g. J-0014, O-V2-003) must never be filed as ACTIVE law; the validator cannot read judgment status semantics, so status: ACTIVE correctness is a Human review duty on the PR.

matter-row.authority_requirements: Human direction to publish the public row (recorded in the authorization receipt's authority field) plus a public-safe determination. The validator checks the authority field is present and non-empty; its substance is Clinton's PR review.
matter-row.description: Representative public matter row (PUB-M-n). Public rows are representative-only and public-safe; the private canonical docket is authoritative.
matter-row.index_coverage: changed files must include docket/matters.json or docket/MATTERS.md
matter-row.matter_rules: The row IS the matter linkage; matter_linkage must be null or the row's own id.
matter-row.notes: Public matter rows are opened only when publication is public-safe and Human-directed. Private evidence travels as PRIVATE_RETAINED opaque pointers, never bodies.

order.authority_requirements: Must cite the Human authority for issuance (the Order itself or the standing authority it is issued under). Every cited Order/Judgment/Rule reference must resolve to an existing record.
order.description: Human Order (general or matter-specific). Filed as law/orders/<id>.md with an INDEX.json row after privacy scrub.
order.index_coverage: changed files must include law/orders/INDEX.json (the discoverability row HC1 mandates)
order.matter_rules: NO matter linkage required (HC2: an unlinked Order is not a defect). If matter_linkage is present it must resolve to an existing matter row.
order.notes: Private-classified orders belong on the private canonical docket, never the public repo; this validator blocks them.

receipt.authority_requirements: The authorization_receipt.authority must reference the original filing's authorization (e.g. 'publication of authorized filing O-...').
receipt.description: Publication receipt (R-...). Filed AFTER publication by the publishing identity: what was published, commit SHA, validator verdict, timestamp. Filed via its own PR through this same gate.
receipt.index_coverage: none required (receipts are append-only; no index row mandated by controlling law)
receipt.matter_rules: NO matter linkage required. If present it must resolve.
receipt.notes: The publication receipt is created after merge, so it cannot ride the PR it records. Its own filing re-enters the gate as a new PR.

standing-order.authority_requirements: Must cite Human adoption (the standing order is adopted by the Human; per-run permission is not required thereafter, but the adoption filing itself needs the Human's content approval).
standing-order.description: Standing Order / Atlas Rule. Same as order, plus the one-sentence rule entry in AR/README.md. Applies to every run automatically once adopted.
standing-order.index_coverage: changed files must include law/orders/INDEX.json AND AR/README.md (the one-sentence rule entry)
standing-order.matter_rules: Must NOT carry a matter number. Standing/procedural Orders stand alone with authority + provenance (HC1). A matter_linkage value is treated as an artificial matter and routes to human review.
standing-order.notes: Rule wording must be one sentence (Human instruction); the validator cannot judge prose length meaningfully, so this remains a Human review duty on the PR.

title: Atlas public-docket filing types (publication gate)
